summary: NIFTY on NSE_INDEX: an index packet at Quote, then with a Depth client too: an index has OHLC and the previous close, no volume, totals, book or OI.

notes: indexData's percentChange and yearly high and low are not read by either side.

Quote to Depth is the same feed type (ALL); the web's adapter calls subscribe_scrips again at ALL and its client sends a second subscribe, and so does the desktop (lead decision, bk-b phase B round 2 item e: the broker-facing frames are part of parity; nothing shows the second subscribe is a no-op at HDFC). An index has no book on either side: neither Depth frame has a depth key.

deviations.reason: An index packet carries no volume, trade quantity, average price or book totals; the web sends them as 0 (its parser's volume 0, the adapter's tick.get(..., 0)) instead of leaving them out. Lead decision (bk-b phase B, item 5): an index's volume, last quantity, average price and book totals are left out; the web's 0 is a web defect.

An index packet carries no trade time; the web falls back to the packet's own time (tick.get('ltt', tick.get('timestamp'))) and sends it as ltt, a time no trade happened at. The desktop leaves ltt out (investright::set_trade_time). Lead decision (bk-b phase B, item 4): the trade-time fallback is absent, never a packet or receipt time.

The HDFC Securities web adapter sends the change as change and change_percent only; the desktop also sends the canonical price_change and price_change_percent. Needs lane wire's canonical-change switch (per-broker key rule: canonical price_change* off for HDFC, change and change_percent kept).
